title: Blest Is the Man Who Fears the Lord
description: Blest Is the Man Who Fears the Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 410 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Influence of Habitual Piety”, where the book credits them to the Exeter Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest is the man who fears the Lord! His well es-tab-lished mind, In ev-ery vary-ing scene of life, Shall true com-po-sure find.

lines: Blest is the man who fears the Lord!
In every varying scene of life,
Oft through the deep and stormy sea
But on a glorious world beyond
His faith can fix its eye.
Though dark his present prospects be,
Yet hope can whisper to his soul,
Full in the presence of his God,
And, fearing him, no other fear

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
